subsection: H. Directors and Officers Liability (D&O) Insurance
text: Thus, the filing of a charge with the EEOC does not constitute a “claim.” [See Bensalem Township v. Western World Ins. Co. (ED PA 1985) 609 F.Supp. 1343, 1347-1348 (applying Penn. law)—complaint filed with EEOC and EEOC's subsequent correspondence to Township advising it of discrimination charge did not constitute a claim because neither requested money or other relief nor advised that a lawsuit was to follow] 3 2) [3:672] FEHA proceedings: The California Department of Fair Employment and Housing (DFEH) has powers of both conciliation and coercion. Upon conclusion of its investigation of a charge of discrimination under the California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA, Gov.C. § 12900 et seq.), the DFEH may seek conciliation; issue a “right to sue” letter to the employee, which is a prerequisite to the filing of a civil action by the employee; or bring a civil action in the name of the DFEH on behalf of the person claiming to be aggrieved (Gov.C. § 12965(a), (c) (amended Stats. 2021, Ch. 278; eff. 1/1/22)).
